title: Neanderthal and Denisovan lines part ways
place: Eurasia; evidence from Sima de los Huesos, Spain
summary: DNA from 430,000-year-old bones at Sima de los Huesos, Spain, sits on the Neanderthal side of the family tree, so Neanderthals and Denisovans had already split before then.
why: Ancient DNA from very old fossils can pin down when branches of the human family separated.
